Title: Arkansas Gov. Signs Amended Religious Freedom Bill
Summary:
In November 2016 Arkansas' Religious Freedom Reformation Act was signed into law by Governor Asa Hutchinson (R). It included several provisions aimed at protecting LGBTQ rights but also included measures intended to address complaints from some religious groups that LGBTQ people face discrimination based on their sexual orientation or gender identity."
"While we are taking all steps necessary pursuant our constitutional duties as elected officials," Hutchinson continued during a news conference announcing his decision not to sign into law an earlier draft of Senate Bill 3-16-1400 ("Arkansas' Marriage Equality Amendment"), "there are certain sections in this measure which are blatantly discriminatory and others which I do not feel are sufficiently neutral." He pointed out three provisions related specifically to LGBTQ people: Section 1 prohibits local governments from passing nondiscrimination ordinances if they include any references about being opposed under religious belief; section 2 prevents cities from enacting civil unions for same-sex couples; and section 3 allows counties — including those with fewer than half their residents identifying as white —to prohibit local public schools from providing affirmative action for students who attend school districts where at least 5 percent of students identify as Asian American or Pacific Islander."
